2608.28447.title: Learning to Use Tools: Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Integrated Mathematical Reasoning
2608.28447.paper_summary: Current large language models (LLMs) increasingly benefit from external tool integration, especially for tasks requiring reliable computation and verification. Motivated by this, we study calculator tool calling for improving mathematical reasoning on the Countdown task. We first analyze reasoning failures and find that calculation errors account for a substantial portion of incorrect responses. We then construct supervised fine-tuning datasets to teach the model useful tool-use patterns and how to interpret returned outputs. Building on this tool-formatted policy, we apply several on-policy reinforcement learning methods, including RLOO, RLOO++, GRPO, and DAPO, using automatically verifiable final-answer rewards. To enable a more reliable evaluation, we construct a fresh 1,024-problem held-out Countdown benchmark with no exact overlap with the training data. Our results show that calculator tool integration consistently improves both SFT and RL baselines, yielding roughly 10 percentage-point gains across pass@k. Among the RL methods, Tool-DAPO achieves the strongest performance, improving pass@1 from 35.8% for Tool-SFT to 66.0%. Further analysis shows that RL encourages more effective tool use even when only final-answer rewards are provided. These findings suggest that tool integration reduces arithmetic and verification errors, while RL increases the probability of correct reasoning traces.
2608.28447.paper_summary_zh: 目前的大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越依賴外部工具的整合，特別是在需要可靠計算和驗證的任務中。受到這一點的啟發，我們研究了計算器工具的調用，以改善倒計時任務中的數學推理。我們首先分析了推理失敗的情況，發現計算錯誤佔據了不正確回應的相當一部分。然後，我們構建了監督式微調數據集，以教會模型有用的工具使用模式以及如何解釋返回的輸出。在這個工具格式的策略基礎上，我們應用了幾種在線強化學習方法，包括RLOO、RLOO++、GRPO和DAPO，使用自動可驗證的最終答案獎勵。為了實現更可靠的評估，我們構建了一個全新的1,024題的保留倒計時基準，與訓練數據沒有精確重疊。我們的結果顯示，計算器工具的整合持續改善了SFT和RL基準，在pass@k上帶來了大約10個百分點的增益。在RL方法中，Tool-DAPO達到了最強的表現，將Tool-SFT的pass@1從35.8%提高到66.0%。進一步的分析顯示，即使僅提供最終答案獎勵，RL也鼓勵了更有效的工具使用。這些發現表明，工具整合減少了算術和驗證錯誤，而RL則提高了正確推理痕跡的概率。
